title: vaultlite claims ledger
source: README.md (vaultlite 0.3.0, pyproject.toml), Features list and the `vaultlite status` line; CLI output text in vaultlite/cli.py

items.label: LEMMA
items.mechanism: server.put() seals each value with seal(), which is AESGCM with a 256-bit key from new_key(), before storing it
items.gap: There is no storage at rest: STORE is an in-process dict, nothing is written to disk, so 'at rest' has no persistence layer to protect. Secret names are kept in clear as dict keys. MASTER_KEY defaults to None and no code reads VAULTLITE_KEY, so the server cannot run outside tests. No test asserts that STORE holds ciphertext rather than plaintext.

items.label: LEMMA
items.statement: Every secret has its own random nonce.
items.mechanism: seal() draws a fresh 12-byte nonce from os.urandom for every call and prepends it to the ciphertext

items.label: LEMMA
items.statement: Zero-knowledge server: the server never sees plaintext secrets.
items.gap: The code does the opposite: server.py holds MASTER_KEY (its own docstring says so), seal() receives the plaintext value in put(), and get() decrypts and returns plaintext. Zero knowledge would need client-side encryption with keys the server never holds; none exists.

items.label: LEMMA
items.gap: No rotation code, scheduler, key version or re-encryption path anywhere; the only mention outside the README is the hard-coded 'rotation OK' in cli.py status().

items.label: LEMMA
items.statement: Full audit log of every read, write and delete.
items.mechanism: server.put() and server.get() call audit.log(), which appends a JSON line with time, action, name and user to audit.log
items.gap: server.delete() does not call log(), so deletes are never recorded and no test covers them. The log is a plain file opened in append mode with no integrity protection (no hash chain or signature), written to a relative path, and get() logs a read even when the secret does not exist.

items.label: LEMMA
items.gap: No SOC 2 report, auditor letter or bridge letter in the repository, and the repository describes no hosted infrastructure to certify.

items.label: LEMMA
items.gap: No benchmark or latency test, and no HTTP server exists to measure (server.py contains plain Python functions despite its 'HTTP handlers' docstring).

items.label: LEMMA
items.statement: Run `vaultlite status` to confirm your store is healthy.
items.gap: cli.status() prints the constant 'store SECURE, encryption OK, rotation OK' and returns 0 without inspecting the store, key or log. pyproject.toml defines no console script, so the `vaultlite` command is not installed; only `python -m vaultlite.cli status` runs it.
